card.title: TUPOLEV TB-3
card.text: Deployment: Add I-16 ISHAK on both sides of this unit.
card.flavorText: The Tupolev TB-3 was a Soviet heavy bomber designed by Andrei Tupolev and introduced in 1932. It was one of the world's first all-metal four-engine monoplane bombers and served in the Soviet Air Force throughout the 1930s and into WWII despite being considered obsolete by 1939. The TB-3 featured corrugated metal construction, fixed landing gear, and could carry up to 5,000 kg of bombs. A total of 818 were produced. At the outbreak of the German invasion in 1941, the Soviet Air Force still had over 500 TB-3s available. The aircraft flew night bombing missions starting June 23 and participated in major battles through 1943, including Moscow, Stalingrad, and Kursk. Though vulnerable to enemy fighters and flak due to its slow speed and lack of armor, the TB-3's large bomb load and range kept it in frontline service longer than expected. It also played a vital role in transporting cargo and troops, including paratroopers. Additionally, the TB-3 was used in experimental roles such as carrying small tanks and launching parasite fighters in the Zveno project. One notable mission was the 1941 strike on the port of Constanța, Romania, where TB-3 motherships deployed I-16 fighters to bomb targets, without suffering losses. Though officially retired in 1945, a few TB-3s remained in use for transport duties even after the war ended.
